note: Every view and projection the Markets Desk has made, newest first, with the news that bears on each, until it is right, wrong or closed. Never delete an entry: a wrong call stays on the record, marked wrong.

views.title: Chip stocks stay under pressure into Apple's results
views.detail: Intel fell 28.6%, Qualcomm 11.1%, Broadcom 5.5% and Nvidia 4.2% on Friday as investors question AI spending; Nvidia is at its lowest since 1 August.

updates.text: Intel guided fourth-quarter revenue to $15bn–$16bn against about $17bn expected; Qualcomm fell 11% and Broadcom 5.5%.
The semiconductor index fell about 3.4% on Monday and Nvidia closed at $202.06, its lowest since 1 August; Apple fell about 3% after hours.

views.title: The hike supports the pound and the banks
views.detail: A 100-basis-point rise pays foreign holders of Egyptian debt to stay, which should cap the dollar and widen banks' margins.
views.wrong: The dollar closes above EGP 57 before the next T-bill auction.

updates.text: The central bank raised its key rates by 100 basis points, to 20.00% for deposits and 21.00% for lending.
The central bank's dollar rate eased to 55.98 to buy and 56.12 to sell at Thursday's close, from 56.06 and 56.20 on Wednesday.
Analysts said the hike aims to preserve the appeal of local debt and limit outflows with the dollar near EGP 56; the dollar stood at 56.12 at the central bank.
Banks begin repricing certificates after the hike; EGP 110bn of bills are at auction today. The dollar is unchanged at EGP 56.12 at the central bank.
The central bank's dollar selling rate fell to EGP 55.86 on Sunday from 56.12.
Central bank dollar rate EGP 55.51 on Monday against 56.04 on 30 October (the pound's leg holds); JPMorgan now sees inflation at 14.3% by year-end and no cuts before the second half of 2027.

views.title: Developers lag while rates stay high
views.detail: Dearer financing hits instalment buyers and developers' own borrowing; Talaat Moustafa and Palm Hills should trail the EGX30.
views.wrong: Talaat Moustafa and Palm Hills beat the EGX30 over four weeks.

updates.text: Talaat Moustafa signed an EGP 11 trillion development deal with the state for four projects.
Al Ahly Pharos put Palm Hills' fair value at EGP 21.40, well above its price.
Talaat Moustafa closed at EGP 79.50 and Palm Hills at EGP 10.60 (−7.0%, lowest since April).
Talaat Moustafa fell 1.9% to EGP 78.00 and Palm Hills was flat at EGP 10.60; both are below their starting levels while the EGX30 is down 2.4%.

views.title: Oil above $110 weighs on the pound
views.detail: Egypt imports much of its fuel, so a dearer barrel adds to the dollars it needs.

updates.text: December Brent rose toward $116 after the Revolutionary Guards said four tankers struck mines in the Strait of Hormuz.
January Brent settled at $113.43 and December at $117.64, a six-month high, after tanker strikes in Hormuz.
Iran says a plan with Qatari mediators to reopen Hormuz within two days is under discussion; a deal would pull Brent down from $113.43.
Brent settled at $113.43 on Friday and traded near $110–112 on Monday as two tankers burned in Hormuz.
January Brent settled at $104.77 on Monday, down 7.6% and below the $110 the call needs, while the pound firmed to EGP 55.51; the premise has lapsed unless oil rebounds.

views.title: Money rotates from AI spenders to steady earners
views.detail: After Alphabet's fall, investors favour predictable earnings (Walmart, JPMorgan) over heavy AI spenders.
views.wrong: Alphabet and Amazon beat Walmart and JPMorgan over four weeks.

updates.text: Amazon and Intel fell after the bell on earnings misses, deepening the AI-spending sell-off.
Money left technology on Friday while Walmart rose 1.9% to $123.51 and Alphabet fell 1.4% to $279.84.
Walmart rose 3.4% to $127.69 (+5.3% since 30 Oct), Visa and Costco rose, Oracle fell 8.8% and chipmakers 3.4%: money moved from AI names to steady earners.

views.title: Amazon trades lower after its miss
views.detail: Earnings of $1.89 a share against $1.97 expected, and revenue just short.
views.wrong: It closes back above $245 within two weeks.

updates.text: Amazon fell about 6% in extended trading after missing on earnings and revenue.
Amazon closed at $240.35 on Friday as AI-related selling spread across the Nasdaq.
Amazon rose 2.2% to $245.63 on Monday, above $245.

result.text: Amazon closed at $245.63 on 2 November, above the $245 level that made the call wrong, within two weeks of its results (from $243.79 on 30 October).

views.title: Higher rates protect CIB's margins
views.detail: High rates protect lending margins and T-bill income; CIB should hold up better than the market.
views.wrong: CIB falls more than the EGX30 over the next two weeks.

updates.text: The central bank raised its key rates by 100 basis points, to 20.00% for deposits and 21.00% for lending.
CIB fell 2.1% to EGP 118.00, its lowest since March, as the EGX30 lost 1.7%.
On Monday the central bank sold the dollar at EGP 55.51 (from 56.04 on 30 Oct) and CIB rose 2.9% to EGP 121.40, above its EGP 120.47 start, though the EGX30 fell to 48,403.

views.title: CIB: bullish, EGP 128–132 by end of December
views.detail: A return to its 50-day average (130.7). The hike widens margins, the stock is 16% below its 52-week high, and it trades near 5.5 times its last reported earnings.
views.wrong: It closes below EGP 114, 5% under Thursday’s close, or the EGX30 falls while it does.

updates.text: The central bank raised its key rates by 100 basis points, to 20.00% for deposits and 21.00% for lending.
CIB closed at EGP 118.00, 8% below the 50-day average the projection targets and above the EGP 114 stop.
CIB closed at EGP 121.40, up 2.9%, as funds concentrated in the most liquid name; the range is EGP 128–132 by end of December.

views.title: Orascom Construction: bullish, EGP 860–900 by end of January
views.detail: Dollar revenue from Gulf and US projects gains from the weaker pound. Up 91% this year, so a pause is as likely as a new high.
views.wrong: It closes below EGP 780, 5% under Thursday, or the pound recovers sharply.

updates.text: OCI shareholders approved the Orascom Construction combination; Amsterdam delisting is set for November (headline-level report).
Orascom Construction expects to complete the OCI merger in December; the stock fell 1.3% to EGP 811.02.
Orascom fell 3.7% to EGP 781, just above the EGP 780 level that would make the call wrong; the OCI merger board meeting is on Thursday.

views.title: Talaat Moustafa: bearish, EGP 72–76 by end of December
views.detail: Down 7.6% in a month and 12% under its 50-day average (91.3); the hike lands on its buyers and its debt. Its EGP 11 trillion state deal is a long-term offset, so confidence is low.
views.wrong: It closes back above EGP 88, near its 50-day average, or a big sales launch beats expectations.

updates.text: Talaat Moustafa signed an EGP 11 trillion development deal with the state.
Talaat Moustafa closed at EGP 79.50, still above the projected EGP 72–76 range.
Talaat Moustafa fell 1.9% to EGP 78.00, its lowest since April, inside sight of the EGP 72–76 range.

views.title: Palm Hills: bearish, EGP 10.2–10.8 by end of December
views.detail: Down 10.6% in a month and 16% under its 50-day average (13.5), under the same rate pressure as Talaat Moustafa. Al Ahly Pharos values it at EGP 21.40 on existing assets alone, which argues against a deep fall.

updates.text: Al Ahly Pharos put Palm Hills' fair value at EGP 21.40.
Palm Hills closed at EGP 10.60, inside the projected EGP 10.2–10.8 range.
Palm Hills was flat at EGP 10.60 after Sunday's 7.0% fall; it is inside the EGP 10.2–10.8 range, due 31 December.

views.title: Abu Qir Fertilizers: bearish, EGP 80–85 by end of November
views.detail: Profit-taking after a 73% run this year: it fell 3.5% on Thursday even as nine-month profit roughly doubled to about EGP 13bn, a sign the good news was priced in. The weaker pound helps its exports, so the downside should be limited.
views.wrong: It makes a new high above EGP 95.75.

updates.text: Nine-month profit roughly doubled to about EGP 13bn, yet the stock fell 3.5%: the results look priced in.
Abu Qir fell 4.0% to EGP 84.55, inside the projected EGP 80–85 range.
Abu Qir fell 4.7% to EGP 80.60, already inside the EGP 80–85 range; judged on 30 November, and the desk drops it from the active list while it sits in range.

views.title: Exxon Mobil: bullish, $185–195 by end of December
views.detail: At its 52-week high and up 52% this year; Friday's results showed profit doubling to $15.4bn. More upside needs Brent to hold above $110.
views.wrong: Brent falls below $100, for example on a Gulf de-escalation.

updates.text: Third-quarter profit doubled to $15.4bn on higher oil prices and record output.
Exxon rose 2.2% to a record $187.25, inside the projected range, with Brent at a six-month high.
Exxon Mobil fell 4.1% to $179.67 as Brent dropped 7.6% to $104.77 on US-Iran deal hopes; wrong if Brent closes below $100.

views.title: Walmart: bullish, $124–128 by end of December
views.detail: Well above its 50-day average (109.8) after the rotation; its 52-week high of 134.20 is the ceiling to watch.
views.wrong: It closes below $115 as money returns to tech.

updates.text: Walmart rose 3.4% to $127.69, at the top of the $124–128 range, due 31 December.

views.title: Amazon: bearish, $225–235 by end of November
views.detail: Missed on earnings ($1.89 against $1.97) and revenue, and fell about 6% after hours, which would take it near 229.
views.wrong: It closes back above $245 within two weeks of the results.

updates.text: Amazon fell about 6% after hours on its earnings miss.
Amazon rose 2.2% to $245.63 on Monday, above $245.

result.text: Amazon closed at $245.63 on 2 November, above the $245 level that made the projection wrong, within two weeks of the results; the $225–235 range was not reached.

views.title: Alphabet: bearish, $265–280 by end of November
views.detail: Already down 17.5% in a month and near its 52-week low (273.50), so much of the bad news is in the price; the risk is further downgrades.

updates.text: UBS cut its price target to $332 from $380 and kept a neutral rating.
Alphabet closed at $279.84, inside the projected $265–280 range, as AI-spending worries spread.
Alphabet raised EUR 6bn in bonds on EUR 17bn of orders and closed at $278.99, inside the $265–280 range.

views.title: Banque du Caire holds above its EGP 5.30 offer price in its first week
views.detail: The retail tranche was 27 times covered, retail buyers can sell back at the offer price for 30 days, and the private placement drew EGP 205.8bn of orders; a weak EGX30 limits any pop.
views.wrong: Banque du Caire trades below EGP 5.30 in its first week.

updates.text: Shares begin trading today; the first session had not opened at the time of writing.
Debut close EGP 5.31 (+0.19%) against the EGP 5.30 offer. It touched EGP 5.25 intraday, below the offer, but closed above it; the view is judged on closes.
